title: Daniel Farber’s place-based theory of standing
shortTitle: Daniel Farber’s place-based theory of standing
summary: The assigned note attributes to Farber a proposed environmental-standing rule based on an appropriate relationship to a specific affected area.
notes:
The casebook briefly summarizes Daniel Farber’s A Place-Based Theory of Standing. Drawing together Massachusetts v. EPA and Laidlaw, Farber proposes that a plaintiff should be able to challenge environmental violations involving a specific area if the plaintiff shows an appropriate relationship to that area.

This is a scholarly simplification of a difficult field. It highlights the practical importance of a claimant’s connection to a place, which also appears in Sierra Club, Lujan, and Laidlaw. The supplied paragraph does not specify every boundary of an appropriate relationship or reproduce the article’s complete argument. It therefore supports a comparative reading and a question about doctrinal coherence, rather than a substitute for the courts’ actual injury, causation, and redressability requirements.
